experience.player_does: Walk continuously through the four-screen world while optionally toggling the F2 grid view and F3 diagnostics.
experience.feels_like: Camera-following movement should stay smooth because static map geometry is rendered once while only a texture transform and circle position change.
experience.camera: The camera keeps following and clamping the circle as before, while a one-shot world-map viewport texture receives the inverse camera translation.
experience.controls: Existing movement, F2 grid, F3 diagnostics, and Escape controls remain unchanged.
experience.not_this: Not a change to movement rules, map appearance, shipping VSync policy, or a native rewrite; this separates static presentation work from per-frame player presentation.

design_refs.why: The fixed fullscreen presentation must remain readable as the authored world grows; runtime measurements make the cost of that presentation observable before changing its implementation.

mockup.not_possible: This slice changes retained rendering work and runtime frame timing without changing the intended visual composition; a static vector picture cannot represent the performance boundary.

considered_existing.why_not: It already owns the screen-level input and draw pass, so the diagnostic panel can stay a small presentation extension rather than adding a second runtime service.
The panel can be drawn in the existing root Control above the translated map, so a new scene node would add structure without improving measurement.
It records the observed performance concern but is testimony rather than a runtime measurement source.
The project setting supplies the current VSync default, but it is engine-owned and the debug slice should report rather than silently change the presentation policy.

It remains the coordinator for input, movement, camera state, and the circle, but its redraw callback is the source of the movement hitch; retaining static map drawing there would rebuild the map on every player update.

modules.role: Coordinate input, movement, camera transforms, and the circle while delegating static map rendering to a one-shot viewport texture.
modules.why: Movement profiling shows that rebuilding the visible map on every player update is the remaining frame-time cost; the node layer should update a texture transform rather than regenerate geometry or process the full world each frame.
modules.boundary_data: Reads typed float and integer monitor values from Engine and Performance, formats them as overlay text, and emits no gameplay state.

revisions.what: Expanded the approved file and function inventory to include the earlier map and movement changes still present in the working tree.
revisions.why: Conformance compares against the commit baseline, so omitting those uncommitted files made the rendered plan report valid existing work as unplanned.

revisions.what: Separated the diagnostics panel from Main and changed the map renderer to avoid idle redraws and merge contiguous background cells.
revisions.why: The reported 4 FPS while stationary was consistent with queue_redraw on every physics tick plus thousands of per-cell background draws; the overlay also needed to update without invalidating the map CanvasItem.

revisions.what: Added a performance-focused follow-up to batch the F2 grid view and report VSync and the software FPS cap in diagnostics.
revisions.why: Runtime sampling showed the normal world path at about 390 FPS with VSync disabled, the old grid path at about 89 FPS with VSync disabled, and the default project VSync enabled; the human also set performance, maintainability, and distribution size as standing priorities.

revisions.what: Implemented the approved gridline batching and cap diagnostics, removing the obsolete per-cell draw helper.
revisions.why: The shared grid boundary path preserves the inspection view while reducing draw calls and keeping the renderer surface free of dead fallback code.

revisions.what: Drafted a static-map rendering slice after profiling movement through the world.
revisions.why: The moving-world sample averaged 59–68 FPS with VSync disabled even though stationary frames were fast, showing that the remaining cost is rebuilding map draw commands whenever the player moves.

revisions.what: Revised the static map from a retained full-world CanvasItem to a one-shot SubViewport texture.
revisions.why: The direct CanvasItem removed script rebuilds but still rasterized the entire four-screen world every frame, measuring 37–60 FPS; a viewport texture keeps the retained render cost out of the movement frame.

revisions.what: Implemented the one-shot SubViewport texture and panned its Sprite2D surface during camera movement.
revisions.why: After warm-up, controlled held movement measured 390–393 FPS uncapped in both normal and F2 grid views; the remaining startup samples were the one-time static texture build.
